The Quora duplicate-detection task is a binary text-pair classification problem whose winning pipeline blends three distinct families — (1) deep Siamese sequence models with attention (Bi-LSTM), (2) gradient-boosted trees on handcrafted lexical/statistical features (XGBoost + n-gram overlap + Jaccard + Magic Features), and (3) graph-structural features derived from the question co-occurrence graph — none of which appear together in any candidate. shopee_price_match_1st is the closest structural relative (pairwise similarity + graph grouping) but is explicitly contraindicated for single-modality input, lacks LSTM/attention stages, and has no GBDT or handcrafted-feature stage. A novel template should combine: (a) a Siamese encoder stage supporting pre-trained word embeddings (GloVe/Word2Vec) plus attention pooling, (b) a handcrafted-feature extraction stage (n-gram overlap, Jaccard, TF-IDF cosine, length ratios, Magic/frequency features), (c) a question-graph construction stage that computes node-degree and other structural features, and (d) a two-stream ensemble stage merging deep and shallow predictions via XGBoost or a linear blender.
